newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel mixed on softer crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel mixed on softer crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were mixed on Monday amid the weak crude market, with physical barrels steady while swaps were lower, traders said.

They said the physical market continued to get support from a Singapore trader who on Monday bought a cargo at $26.30 per barrel from a European major for May 24-28 lifting free-on-board (fob), and another from a Swiss trader at $26.70 for May 13-17 lifting, unchanged from last Friday.
Some buying support for gas oil was seen from Nepal, Sri Lanka and India for May and June deliveries, while Bangladesh seeks kerosene for end-May delivery.
But traders said India's projected purchase in its June tender is limited to around 600,000 tonnes, compared with 870,000 tonnes for May deliveries.
Jet fuel was traded higher with a US trader selling to a Singapore trader at $24.50 per barrel for May 13-17, up 40 cents from Friday's deal.
The trader has bought nearly three million barrels of jet fuel over the past two months which was helping to hold prices from spiralling downwards at a time of soft regional demand.
Swaps gas oil dipped by 25 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $25.55/$25.65 for May.
